newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Taiwan's First Commercial Bank.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Taiwan's First Commercial Bank.

text.p: IBCA the European credit rating agency said on Monday it assigned an individual rating of B/C to First Commercial Bank of Taiwan (FCB).
"First Commercial's previously assigned Legal rating of 2 remains unchanged," IBCA said in a statement.
"FCB is one of the three large, majority government owned commercial banks operating in Taiwan, where it commands an approximately six percent share of both the loan and deposit markets," IBCA said.

"First Commercial's performance, capitalisation and financial profile are satisfactory, although its profitability was impacted in fiscal 1995 by losses resulting from its derivative activities. Like most banks in Taiwan, it is experiencing a decline in its asset quality, but from a high level by relative standards," said IBCA.

"Market share has also declined as a consequence of competition from the newly established private banks, but its majority government shareholding and extensive branch network should ensure that its deposit base remains stable." IBCA said.

IBCA's individual rating is an evaluation of the bank's financial strength based on the premise that it is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners. The highest individual rating awarded by IBCA is A. Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if it ran into difficulties, IBCA said.
